$$

First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following trigonometric identity:

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{coth}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{3}}\operatorname{coth}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{3}}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this by substitution. Let $u=\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x.$ Then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we fill the table for the limits of integration, according to the rule $u=\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x.$

| $x$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ |

Now, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{2}}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡\sqrt{3}}\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡2x}{\operatorname{sinh}⁡2x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3/4}^{4/3}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{3/4}^{4/3}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|{|}_{3/4}^{4/3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{3}{4})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})\end{aligned}
$$
